claims.text: DFT with phonon-dispersion calculations can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed DFT approach will improve predictive accuracy by 15–25% over current empirical or simplified predictions.
DFT with phonon-dispersion calculations explicitly accounts for complex phonon-phonon interactions and scattering rates.
Complex phonon-phonon interactions and scattering rates dominate thermal transport in high-entropy alloys.
Phonon dispersion relations, lifetimes, and scattering rates determine phonon thermal conductivity and enable more accurate thermal-transport predictions.
The proposed approach will predict phonon thermal conductivity values at least 20% lower than current predictions.
Candidate high-entropy alloys identified by the approach will have thermal conductivity of 1.5 W m^-1 K^-1 or lower at 500 K.
Explicit treatment of phonon-phonon interactions is expected to reduce predicted thermal conductivity by 15–30% relative to empirical models.
The approach is applicable between 300 K and 1000 K and at pressures no greater than 1 atm.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys containing no more than five constituent elements and having a mixing entropy of at least 1.5R.
Alloys with more than five elements or mixing entropy below 1.5R may have more complex phase behavior or greater deviations from ideal-solution behavior.
Complex phase behavior or deviation from ideal-solution behavior would limit the accuracy of the DFT-based approach.
Predictive accuracy may depend on the exchange-correlation functional, calculation convergence, and quality of validation data.
A measured thermal conductivity more than 15% above the DFT-predicted value would falsify the hypothesis.
The hypothesis would also be falsified if at least 75% of the tested alloys have measured thermal conductivities within 10% of current predictions.
